messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most rural roads, 35 mph on most urban roads.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or special circumstances. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children 8–15 must be in a seat belt or booster. | Failure to buckle up can result in a fine of $50–$100. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and for drivers under 21 (0.02 %).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time, mandatory alcohol‑education programs. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” policy for drivers under 21. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Violations carry a fine of $50–$100. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• Stop signs: must come to a complete stop before proceeding. | Failure to yield can lead to traffic citations or liability in accidents. | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during any weather that reduces visibility.
• Fog lights may be used in fog, rain, or snow. | Failure to use headlights when required can result in a fine. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing of vehicles requires a valid permit and proper equipment. | Unregistered vehicles can be impounded. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking on the curb is prohibited in many areas. | Violations can result in towing and fines. | | **School Bus Rules** | • When a school bus stops and its red lights flash, all vehicles must stop.
• On two‑lane roads, only vehicles traveling in the opposite direction must stop. | Failure to stop can lead to heavy fines and points on your license. | | **Points System** | • Texas uses a points system for traffic violations.
• Accumulating 4 points in 12 months can lead to license suspension. | Points are removed after 12 months of no violations. | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Many cities use speed cameras and red‑light cameras.
• Violations are mailed to the registered owner. | Fines can be higher than manual citations. | | **Special Zones** | • Construction zones: speed limits may be reduced by 10–20 mph.
• School zones: speed limits may be reduced by 10 mph. | Drivers must obey posted signs. | ### How to Find Specific Laws - **Texas Transportation Code**: The primary source for all traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)**: Offers guides, FAQs, and downloadable handbooks. - **Local County Websites**: Some counties publish additional ordinances (e.g., parking restrictions). ### Quick Resources - **Texas DPS Traffic Law Handbook** – PDF available on the DPS website. - **Texas.gov** – Official state portal with links to traffic regulations. - **Texas Vehicle Code** – Online searchable database. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific rule or how to handle a particular situation!
